problem: Prior human-to-robot learning targets parallel grippers or uses kinematic retargeting that ignores hand-object interaction. RL-based dexterous methods use limited motion sources, per-task rewards, and state-based sim2real that cannot generalize visually. Navigation foundation models such as ViNT are too imprecise to hand off to manipulation.
motivation: Human motion data is abundant, but turning it into physically feasible, visually generalizable bimanual dexterous behaviors on a mobile robot in the wild is unsolved. Navigation and manipulation also need to be bridged, because small final-pose errors make manipulation policies fail.
key_idea: Use one-shot human motion from multiple sources with a unified RL reward, distill it into a depth-based visual policy with hybrid sim2real control, and add closed-loop PnP refinement to ViNT for precise navigation-to-manipulation handoff.
insight: RL with the object-centric distance chain reward turns retargeted trajectories that fail under pure kinematic replay (0% success) into working policies (78.1% for video tasks, 88.9% for mocap tasks). Real-world gains come from the depth preprocessing (67.8% vs 13.3% for raw depth) and from PnP refinement (+54.0% mobile manipulation over ViNT alone), showing that alignment precision is the bottleneck when combining navigation and manipulation.
method: One-shot human motion collection: sim teleoperation with Apple Vision Pro, OakInk2 mocap, and video extraction (WiLoR + PnP for hands, FoundationPose for objects). Trajectories are augmented by randomizing object poses, then retargeted with DexPilot.
Unified reward: object-centric distance chain (fingertip/palm-to-object vectors, gated by contact count), object trajectory tracking, and a power penalty; the same terms are reused across tasks.

Residual action learning: arm action = coarse action from the human trajectory + a learned residual; hand actions come fully from the network. Early termination is used, and object collisions are disabled early in training. Trained with DrM (off-policy) or PPO on MJX.

Depth-based sim2real: clipped depth, Gaussian noise/blur, 0.5% dropout to max depth, and mixup with NYU depth maps. Uses DAgger distillation to a visual student (first 2 ResNet-18 layers with GroupNorm, 3 stacked 140x140 frames), with an exponentially decayed expert rollout probability.

Hybrid sim2real control: the policy infers actions from real observations, a simulated robot (with no objects) steps with the same IK and dynamics, and the resulting joint positions are sent to the real robot.

ViNT + closed-loop PnP: ViNT navigates over long distances to the goal. Efficient LoFTR matches the current image to the goal RGB-D image, RANSAC PnP gives the relative pose, and sequential PID control (x, y, then yaw) iterates until the error falls below a threshold.

setting.backbone: DrM/PPO state-based RL teacher; ResNet-18 (first 2 layers) depth student via DAgger; ViNT (frozen) for navigation; Efficient LoFTR + PnP for localization
setting.training_data: One human reference trajectory per task (teleop, OakInk2 mocap, or video), augmented in simulation; RL in MuJoCo/MJX; NYU Depth for mixup; 5 extra real rollouts for fine-tuning on 2 tasks
setting.observation: egocentric depth (RealSense L515, 140x140) + proprioception for manipulation; RGB (fisheye) for ViNT; RGB-D goal image for PnP
setting.action_space: 6D end-effector pose for arms (coarse + residual) plus dexterous hand joints; planar base velocity (x, y, yaw) for navigation; ViNT waypoints
setting.privileged: Teacher policy uses privileged state (object pose, reference trajectory) in training only; a goal RGB-D image of the target location is captured at test time; none otherwise

numbers_note: Not a standard VLN/navigation-benchmark paper. Results are on custom real-world manipulation and localization tests, and no canonical benchmark metrics are reported. Mobile manipulation results appear only as a bar figure.
results: Real-world zero-shot bimanual dexterous manipulation reaches 67.8% average success over 6 tasks (15 trials each), versus 13.3% for raw depth. Closed-loop PnP cuts localization error to 1.3-3.2 cm (vs 7.3-18 cm for ViNT) and improves mobile manipulation success by 54.0% over ViNT alone. RL also outperforms kinematic retargeting (0%) and trajectory replay (91.9 vs 52.2 on Bottle Handover).
limitations: Tasks are quasi-static; the hybrid control needs system identification for highly dynamic tasks.
Manual tuning of collision parameters and primitive-shape approximations is required, and hardware calibration mismatches lower success rates.
Each task needs its own RL and distillation, and some tasks (pour teapot, putoff burner) needed real-world fine-tuning.
